- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% of recent range.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model often overshoots; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns positive after prolonged negative streak, model underreacts; increase forecast slope by 0.2–0.5% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates volatility in low-sentiment periods; add 0.3–0.7% buffer to forecast if sentiment < -0.4 for 5+ days.
- Lagged response: if sentiment shifts sharply 2–3 days before forecast horizon, model often misses it; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment change.
